newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MILLER LEADS PACERS PAST CELTICS WITH BUZZER-BEATER.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MILLER LEADS PACERS PAST CELTICS WITH BUZZER-BEATER.

text.p: Reggie Miller drained a three-point buzzer-beater to lift the Pacers to a 97-94 victory over the Boston Celtics on Friday, ending Indiana's three-game losing streak.

With the game apparently headed for overtime, Miller took an inbounds pass from Vincent Askew with 1.2 seconds left, turned around and released his shot with just one-tenth of a second on the clock. The ball swished through the net as the final buzzer sounded.
"I told Vince after the timeout to look for me," Miller said. "I think he saw I was wide open and he made a great pass. I got a great look. I couldn't ask for a better look."
Miller, the Pacers' go-to guy at crunch time, finished with 25 points, including 15 in the final period.
"He stepped up and hit the big one," Boston coach M.L. Carr said of Miller. "I thought we did a good job on him in the first half. He hit the big shot at the end."
Derrick McKey contributed 17 points, seven rebounds and seven assists as the Pacers erased a seven-point third-quarter deficit with a season-best 35-point fourth quarter.
David Wesley scored 18 points, Eric Williams added 17 and nine rebounds and Dino Radja scored 14 points for Boston.
At Los Angeles, Shaquille O'Neal scored eight of his 34 points in overtime, including a go-ahead layup with 16 seconds left, to give the Lakers to a 120-119 victory over the Portland Trail Blazers.
O'Neal, who blocked a shot with 1.4 seconds remaining, had 10 rebounds, seven assists and six blocks as the Lakers won for the ninth time in their last 11 games.
Nick Van Exel had 26 points and 15 assists for the Lakers, while Kenny Anderson scored 34 points, Rasheed Wallace chipped in 29 and Clifford Robinson contributed 18 for Portland.
At New Jersey, Michael Jordan scored 22 of his 32 points in the first half as the Chicago Bulls opened a 27-point lead and cruised to a 113-92 victory over the Nets.
Scottie Pippen scored 24 points and Ron Harper added 12 for the Bulls, who won without suspended forward Dennis Rodman and injured centre Luc Longley to improve to 19-3.
Robert Pack scored 25 points to lead the Nets, who played without forward Jayson Williams, who currently leads the NBA in rebounding but sat out with a sprained thumb.
The hot-shooting Bulls led 62-40 at intermission and were up by at least 18 points the rest of the way.
At Washington, Chris Webber had 25 points and 11 rebounds and Jaren Jackson hit a crucial three-pointer with 50 seconds left to lead the Bullets past the Denver Nuggets, 108-104.
Juwan Howard added 22 points and Rod Strickland chipped in 18 points and 12 assists for the Bullets.
Dale Ellis had 22 points and Mark Jackson added 15 and dished out 18 assists for the floundering Nuggets, who have dropped nine straight and 13 of their last 14 games.

At Minnesota, Tom Gugliotta scored 12 of his 25 points in the fourth quarter and drilled a jumper from the corner with 16 seconds left as the Timberwolves snapped a six-game losing streak with a 108-105 victory over the Phoenix Suns.
Stephon Marbury had 21 points and 10 assists, Doug West added 15 points and Sam Mitchell contributed 13 for Minnesota, which beat Phoenix for just the third time in 30 meetings.
Sam Cassell scored 21 points before fouling out and Danny Manning and John Williams added 19 apiece for Phoenix, which had its five-game winning streak snapped.

In Charlotte, Glen Rice scored five of his 24 points on free throws in the final two minutes and five different players hit layups in a decisive 10-2 fourth-qaurter run as the Hornets beat the Philadelphia 76ers 84-75.

Charlotte, which got 20 points and 11 rebounds from Vlade Divac, posted its fourth straight win and sent the Sixers to their sixth consecutive defeat. Anthony Mason chipped in 13 points and 13 rebounds for Charlotte.
Philadelphia, led by Derrick Coleman's 20 points, played without rookie sensation Allen Iverson, who did not travel with the team because of an injured left shoulder.
In Cleveland, Bobby Sura scored 22 points, including four in a decisive fourth-quarter run, and Tyrone Hill added 20 as the Cavaliers rolled past the Golden State Warriors 101-87.
Bobby Phills had eight points and Terrell Brandon six during the 23-8 Cavalier run that turned a one-point deficit into a comfortable 14-point victory.
Latrell Sprewell scored 22 points and Chris Mullin added 21 for the Warriors, who have not beaten the Cavs since 1992.
In the second half Cleveland hit 26-of-29 free throws, while the Warriors made just four.

In Vancouver, Bryant Reeves scored 27 points and rookie Shareef Abdur-Rahim added 21 points and 11 rebounds as the Grizzlies snapped a three-game losing streak with a 95-93 victory over the injury-plagued Orlando Magic.
Rony Seikaly had 25 points and 12 rebounds and Gerald Wilkins added 15 points for Orlando, which again played without injured starters Penny Hardaway and Nick Anderson.
The Magic went on a late 7-3 run to draw within 92-91 with 13 seconds to go but the Grizzlies held on for just their fourth win in 22 games this season.
